data.narrative:
CubeFabs, a Series E frontier-chip company founded by Matthew Putman (PhD, former Columbia materials science professor) and his father John, has raised approximately $182M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 3 public semiconductors peers (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private-stage companies including Etched, Ayar Labs, and Cerebras.

Two triangulation methods are applicable. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.4x step-up multiplier typical of Series E advancement to the $182M total raised proxy, implying $255M. Peer-median anchoring uses three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables—Etched ($5.0B Series E), Ayar Labs ($3.8B Series E), and Tenstorrent ($2.7B Series D)—yielding a median valuation of $3.8B with a range of $2.7B to $5.0B. Public-comp P/S anchoring is inapplicable; the public semiconductor sector median P/S of 20.5x cannot be applied without disclosed revenue from the target.

The triangulated range spans $217M (low) to $4.3B (high), with a median of $2.0B across the two applicable methods. The wide range reflects a fundamental tension: stage-progression conservatively anchors to capital deployed, while peer-median reflects valuations of later-stage or better-capitalized competitors. Key uncertainties include CubeFabs' revenue traction relative to named peers and the sustainability of recent frontier-chip valuations.
